title: Revisiting the Rules-versus-Discretion Debate: Forecasting Evidence from the Bank of England, 1870-1913
abstract: arXiv:2609.10544v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Under the classical gold standard, historians have long debated what guided the Bank of England's adjustments to Bank Rate: whether policy followed a mechanical gold-standard rule or discretion when City or exchange conditions required it, and whether domestic money-market stability or external convertibility carried greater weight. This paper revisits those questions with a London-specific monthly panel, 1870-1913, jointly testing ten domestic and external indicators the Court watched when setting the published minimum rate.   The findings fit neither a single frozen channel nor unstructured ad hoc policy. Instead, the Bank appears to have drawn repeatedly on a multivariate information set-trade settlement, gold movements, City asset prices, bill-market conditions, and episodic convertibility pressure-with state-dependent weights across subperiods. translated_title: 重温“规则与相机抉择”之争：来自英格兰银行1870—1913年的预测证据
translated_abstract: 在古典金本位制下，历史学家长期争论是什么引导了英格兰银行对银行利率（Bank Rate）的调整：政策究竟是遵循机械的金本位规则，还是在伦敦金融城或外汇状况需要时采取相机抉择，以及国内货币市场稳定与外部可兑换性孰轻孰重。本文利用1870—1913年针对伦敦的月度面板数据重新审视这些问题，联合检验了银行理事会在设定公布的最低利率时所关注的十项国内与外部指标。研究发现既不符合单一固化的传导渠道，也不符合无结构的临时性政策。相反，英格兰银行似乎反复依赖一个多变量信息集——包括贸易结算、黄金流动、金融城资产价格、票据市场状况以及间歇性的可兑换性压力——并在不同子时期采用随状态变化的权重。在验证性设定中，出口、黄金流动和工业股票价格承担……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究利用1870—1913年伦敦月度数据发现，英格兰银行的利率政策既非机械的金本位规则也非纯粹的相机抉择，而是基于包含贸易结算、黄金流动、金融城资产价格、票据市场状况等多变量信息集，并在不同历史时期动态调整各指标的权重。
en_tdlr: Using a London-specific monthly panel from 1870–1913, this paper shows that the Bank of England's Bank Rate policy followed neither a rigid gold-standard rule nor unstructured discretion, but instead drew on a multivariate information set—trade settlement, gold movements, City asset prices, and bill-market conditions—with state-dependent weights across subperiods.
